raw_message.reasoning:
I see. So when there's no specific type handler, it falls through to `elif type:` which creates a regex like `\X+` where X is the type character. And if neither type nor precision is set, it uses `(.*?)`.

Now I understand the issue. When using `{:<}` or `{:^}`, the type character `<` or `^` is being used as the type itself (not as alignment). The regex becomes `\<+` or `\^+` which would match literal `<` or `^` characters.
